paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The LORD sees every nation, and no height, no wealth and no fruitful valley puts anyone out of His reach. Ammon trusted in riches and said, "Who can come against me?" Edom perched up in the rocks like an eagle's nest, and the LORD said, "even from there I will bring you down" (Jeremiah 49:4, 16).

Pride is a bad landlord, baker. It tells you the walls are thick and the view is great, and then it sends you the bill. I once bragged about a batch so hard I dropped the whole tray mid-sentence, so I know how that goes. The LORD asks, "who is like Me, and who can challenge Me?" and that question settles it (Jeremiah 49:19).

But look at what else is tucked in there. Right in the middle of Edom's ruin, the LORD says, "Abandon your orphans; I will preserve their lives. Let your widows trust in Me" (Jeremiah 49:11). And after Ammon's fall comes one little word, "Yet afterward I will restore the Ammonites from captivity" (Jeremiah 49:6). So trust the LORD more than your own riches or your own high place, because He is both the One who brings the proud down and the One who watches over the ones with nobody else.
